SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349                                        BEFORE THE STATE
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                                                OFFICE
                                                                    OF
JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR                                          ADMINISTRATIVE
ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC                                       HEARINGS
AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES
CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR
CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND
NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY
EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION
LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,
CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,
LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH,
MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA,
SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND
WILLIAMSON COUNTIES


   INTERVENOR AARON EDWARD HOWTON'S OBJECTION TO APPLICANTS'
              REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF CASEY D. PETTY

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:


       COMES NOW, Aaron Edward Howton, Intervenor in the above-captioned proceeding,

and files this Intervenor's Objection to Applicants' Rebuttal Testimony of Casey D. Petty, filed

on May 28, 2026, in PUC Interchange Item No. 5212, and respectfully shows as follows:


                                     I. INTRODUCTION
   1. Intervenor objects to the portion of Mr. Casey D. Petty's Rebuttal Testimony addressing

       whether Applicants were required to host another public participation meeting for

       landowners affected by newly added or modified routes, including Links F04 and F20.

   2. On page 7 of Mr. Petty's Rebuttal Testimony, Mr. Petty is asked: "Did Applicants host a

       public Participation Meeting for Landowners affected by new routes?" Mr. Petty answers

       “No” and in substance, that Applicants did not host another public meeting because 16

       TAC § 22.52 requires only one public meeting, that additions or modifications are




                                             Page 1
    standard practice after interactions with landowners, and that it is not standard practice to

   host another public meeting for landowners newly affected by added or modified routes.

3. Intervenor objects to this testimony because it improperly suggests that the Applicants'

   "standard practice" is sufficient to satisfy the public-participation purpose of the

   Commission's rules, even when newly added links directly affect a different group of

   landowners who were not given the same meaningful pre-filing opportunity to participate

   as landowners affected by routes presented at the original public meeting.


                      II. FACTUAL BASIS FOR OBJECTION
4. Applicants' own filing in PUC Interchange Item No. 65, including Table 6-1 and Figure

   6-5, states that Links F04 and F20 were added as alternative routes to avoid a large-scale

   proposed development between FM 2843 and a potential future highway.

5. Links F04 and F20 were added after the June 2025 public participation meeting. No

   subsequent public participation meeting was announced or held before Applicants filed

   their CCN application.

6. As a result, landowners newly affected by Links F04 and F20 were deprived of the same

   meaningful opportunity to provide information, identify land-use impacts, and request

   route modifications before the application was filed.

7. The prejudice caused by this process is not theoretical. Landowner John Giddings, on

   behalf of JAG El Rio, LLC, Tract No. 5646, filed sworn direct testimony in PUC

   Interchange Item No. 4431 on May 13, 2026. His testimony states that Link F20 crosses

   his property, and that his land had already been surveyed and platted for a housing

   development. He provided Exhibit A, a survey, and Exhibit B, a plat for seventeen two-

   acre lots.



                                          Page 2
 8. Landowner Leonard Rodell, on behalf of Salado 137, LLC, Tract No. 5650, filed direct

   testimony in PUC Interchange Item No. 4031 on May 13, 2026. His testimony states that

   Link F20 crosses property planned for an eighty-nine-lot, one-acre single-family

   residential development, and he provided Exhibit A showing an overlay of proposed Link

   F20 through the middle of the proposed development.

9. These facts are directly relevant because Applicants state that F04 and F20 were added to

   avoid a proposed development, yet Link F20 was then routed through or across two other

   proposed housing developments whose landowners did not receive the same pre-filing

   public participation opportunity.

10. Had Applicants held a supplemental public meeting after adding Links F04 and F20,

   Applicants would have had an opportunity to learn of these proposed developments

   before filing their application and before presenting Link F20 as part of their alternative

   routing structure.


           III. LEGAL AND PROCEDURAL BASIS FOR OBJECTION
11. The public participation requirement in 16 TAC § 22.52 is not intended to be a mere

   formality. It exists so affected landowners may receive notice and have a meaningful

   opportunity to provide information before the route is finalized for filing.

12. While Mr. Petty states that 16 TAC § 22.52 requires only one public meeting, the facts

   here show that the group of landowners directly affected by Links F04 and F20 changed

   after the public meeting. The newly affected landowners did not receive the same

   opportunity afforded to landowners affected by routes presented at the June 2025 public

   meeting.




                                          Page 3
 13. Intervenor does not object merely because Applicants modified preliminary links.

   Intervenor objects because Applicants modified the links in a way that created new

   directly affected landowners and then relied on "standard practice" to justify not giving

   those newly affected landowners the same opportunity to participate in the pre-filing

   routing process.

14. 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) requires an application for a new transmission line to address

   PURA § 37.056(c) criteria and, considering those criteria, engineering constraints, and

   costs, to route the line to the extent reasonable to moderate the impact on affected

   communities and landowners unless grid reliability and security dictate otherwise.

15. Mr. Petty's testimony fails to adequately address the unequal effect of the Applicants'

   process on the newly affected landowners along Links F04 and F20. The testimony also

   fails to explain why it is reasonable to use a new link to avoid one proposed development

   while placing that same new link through or across other proposed residential

   developments that were not meaningfully considered through a supplemental public

   meeting.

16. Link F20 also places a proposed 765-kV transmission line within approximately 575 feet

   of First Cedar Valley Baptist Church, a historic church established in 1942 where

   community members continue to worship. The placement of a 765-kV transmission line

   so close to this church raises serious concerns regarding community values, historical and

   aesthetic values, and the impact on a community that suffered tornado damage only a few

   years ago and is still rebuilding.

17. Mr. Petty's statement that it is "not standard practice" to host another public meeting for

   newly affected landowners is not a sufficient basis for the Commission or the




                                          Page 4
    Administrative Law Judges to disregard the unequal treatment and prejudice caused by

   adding Links F04 and F20 after the original public meeting.

18. A utility's internal or customary practice cannot override the purpose of the Commission's

   public-participation rules, the requirement to meaningfully consider affected landowners,

   or the routing criteria requiring moderation of impacts on communities and landowners.


                                    IV. OBJECTION
19. Intervenor objects to Mr. Petty's rebuttal testimony to the extent it asks the

   Administrative Law Judges or the Commission to accept Applicants' failure to hold a

   supplemental public meeting for newly affected landowners as fair, adequate, or

   consistent with the intent of 16 TAC § 22.52 and 16 TAC § 25.101.

20. Intervenor further objects to any suggestion that "standard practice" is sufficient evidence

   that the process was fair to landowners newly affected by Links F04 and F20.

21. Intervenor objects to the testimony because it is incomplete, misleading, and fails to

   address material facts regarding the proposed developments on Tracts 5646 and 5650, the

   impact on First Cedar Valley Baptist Church, and the disparate treatment of landowners

   who were affected only after the June 2025 public meeting.

22. Intervenor respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges give little or no

   weight to Mr. Petty's testimony on this issue, or alternatively require Applicants to

   supplement their testimony and routing analysis to address the newly affected

   landowners, the proposed developments, and the lack of a supplemental public meeting

   after Links F04 and F20 were added.


                               V. REQUESTED RELIEF




                                           Page 5
 WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor Aaron Edward Howton respectfully

requests that the Administrative Law Judges:

   1. Sustain this objection to the portions of Mr. Petty's Rebuttal Testimony concerning the

       lack of a supplemental public participation meeting for landowners affected by newly

       added or modified routes;

   2. Find that Mr. Petty's reliance on "standard practice" does not resolve the fairness, notice,

       public participation, and routing concerns raised by the addition of Links F04 and F20

       after the June 2025 public meeting;

   3. Give little or no weight to Mr. Petty's testimony to the extent it suggests Applicants'

       failure to hold a supplemental public meeting was adequate or non-prejudicial;

   4. Require Applicants to supplement their routing analysis regarding Links F04 and F20,

       including the impacts on Tract No. 5646, Tract No. 5650, the proposed residential

       developments, First Cedar Valley Baptist Church, and the Cedar Valley community;

   5. Consider removing Links F04 and F20 from further consideration, or alternatively extend

       appropriate procedural protections to newly affected landowners; and

   6. Grant Intervenor such other and further relief to which he may be justly entitled.


Respectfully submitted,
Aaron Edward Howton
Intervenor

Salado, Texas 76571
